title: Inspect and configure Nucleus quota admission
summary: Read the cached Codex weekly admission condition and interpret its thresholds, freshness, pending-work deferral, and recovery.
use_when: Codex weekly admission, quota_deferred, quota_exhausted, unknown allowance, or startup quota policy must be interpreted.
do_not_use_when: The goal is a quota reset, requester retry, model billing calculation, or clearance of an independent service halt.
outcome: The cached quota condition or configured admission policy is understood through Nucleus-owned state.
effects: Quota reads start no model work. A startup policy controls new main-Codex admission and pending execution.
Nucleus retains quota condition state and samples the external Codex allowance; started attempts continue during a pause.
authority: Nucleus owns quota admission and condition identity; Codex owns the shared account allowance.
Requesters own pending work, deadlines, domain success, and retry decisions. EMT owns shared notices and Email owns transport.
success: The supported quota response identifies the retained condition; recovery requires a fresh qualifying observation rather than reset time alone.
failure_and_recovery: Preserve pending work and exact request identity on deferral. Inspect domain effects after exhaustion before another attempt.
Do not edit quota-state.json to simulate recovery or clear unrelated holds, pauses, or failure halts.
privacy: quota-policy.json and quota-state.json are private mode-0600 regular files beside nucleus.db and belong in Nucleus backups.
Retained quota state includes an account-identity digest, allowance observations, timestamps, and condition identity.

interfaces.label: Read HTTP quota
interfaces.invocation: GET /v1/quota over the Nucleus Unix socket

does_not_authorize: A quota reset, rollout, service restart, replay of expired work, or clearance of existing service halts.
An additional notice send or application retry.

consumers.statement: Operators and requester applications may inspect and obey Nucleus's cached main-Codex weekly admission condition.

preconditions.statement: Use the Nucleus-owned account observation and private startup policy/state; requesters do not duplicate allowance checks or access the canonical credential.

inputs.statement: quota-policy.json beside nucleus.db supplies enabled, pauseAtRemainingPercent, and resumeAboveRemainingPercent at daemon startup, with 0 <= pause < resume < 100.
The account observation selects rateLimitsByLimitId.codex and one weekly windowDurationMins=10080; the legacy limitId=codex bucket is used only when the map is absent. Spark is never substituted.

outputs.statement: GET /v1/quota returns the cached condition without model work. New rejected work receives HTTP 429 quota_deferred with snapshot details and no job/attempt; the Rust client exposes ClientError::QuotaDeferred.
Pending main-Codex job reads attach the condition and get_job_for_work returns typed deferral. Structured usageLimitExceeded ends an attempt with quota_exhausted and immediately pauses admission.

data_semantics.statement: Default policy pauses at 10 percent remaining or less and reopens only above 15 percent after a fresh observation. API-key authentication has no subscription weekly gate.
Absent, null, ambiguous, expired, or malformed weekly data is unknown, not zero or unlimited. Invalid/unavailable data pauses admission unless a valid cached observation remains.

identity_and_units.statement: Remaining percent is 100 minus usedPercent. Observation/reset times are Unix seconds; missing numeric values remain null. One condition ID identifies a continuous pause and state includes an account-identity digest and limitId.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Nucleus samples every 60 seconds. An observation is valid for at most 120 seconds and never past its reset time. Reset time alone does not reopen admission.
Other sessions consume the same account allowance. The threshold reserves no tokens and cannot guarantee completion of active work.
No billing-equivalence or service-availability objective is promised.

access.statement: The supported standard surfaces are the current-user CLI and version-one HTTP protocol over Nucleus's filesystem-protected Unix socket.
Local filesystem ownership and permissions protect the socket and private state; version one has no application-level authentication protocol.
No TCP endpoint, cross-user service, catalog-granted access, or direct SQLite integration is supported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Exact replay of an admitted request remains available. Accepted jobs recheck quota before execution and retain their pending attempt without a slot or running timeout while paused. Started attempts continue.

Reads, cancellation, mailbox responses, and authentication remain available. Scheduled deferral preserves work as an explicit expected outcome, not an abend; deadlines and selection rules remain requester-owned.

Quota state is written atomically and survives restart; an account change requires a new observation. Daemon restart still marks unfinished attempts lost, including pending jobs. Quota recovery clears no other hold, pause, or halt.

operational_limits.statement: Policy and state must be private regular files mode 0600; invalid files prevent startup and both belong in private backups.
No automatic retry, expired-work replay, quota reset, or delivery proof follows from a quota condition.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Upgrade requester clients before enabling the gate and use coordinated maintenance. Clients tolerate a daemon without optional quota health fields; EMT tolerates an old quota endpoint 404. Successful installation can preserve quota-paused admission.

reliances.statement: Quota relies on the external Codex weekly allowance through Nucleus's credential authority; no installed Chancery contract covers upstream account behavior.
